question_text: In distributed transaction protocols, how does the 3-Phase Commit (3PC) protocol improve upon 2-Phase Commit (2PC)?

options.text: It removes network latency by bypassing coordinator consensus
It adds a Pre-Commit phase and bounded timeouts to eliminate indefinite blocking when the coordinator crashes during decision commit
It enables asynchronous eventual consistency across partitions
It allows transactions to commit without write-ahead logs

answer_explanation: 2PC is a blocking protocol: if the coordinator crashes after participants vote Yes, participants must wait indefinitely. 3PC introduces Pre-Commit state, allowing nodes to reach timeout agreement.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: 2PC is a blocking protocol: if the coordinator crashes after participants vote Yes, participants must wait indefinitely. 3PC introduces Pre-Commit state, allowing nodes to reach timeout agreement.
